title: When Missingness Follows the Graph: Beyond Feature Propagation for Missing Features
abstract: arXiv:2610.18113v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) commonly assume that node features are fully observed, despite missing features being pervasive in real-world applications. By leveraging the dependence between node features and graph structure, existing graph-specific methods handle missingness by propagating observed feature values along graph edges. However, these methods have mainly been evaluated in overly optimistic settings, where feature entries are removed independently and uniformly across the graph. This overlooks realistic scenarios in which missingness propagates among connected nodes, as can occur during localized sensing failures in sensor networks. We formalize this complementary notion as graph-structured mask dependence, where the joint distribution of missingness indicators is shaped by the graph, and introduce a controlled mechanism that instantiates this setting. We study propagation-based methods theoretically and empirically in this

translated_title: 当缺失遵循图结构：超越缺失特征的特征传播方法
translated_abstract: 图神经网络（GNNs）通常假设节点特征是完全可观测的，尽管在现实应用中特征缺失普遍存在。通过利用节点特征与图结构之间的依赖关系，现有的图特定方法通过沿图边传播已观测的特征值来处理缺失问题。然而，这些方法主要是在过于乐观的设置下进行评估的，即特征条目在整个图中被独立且均匀地移除。这忽略了缺失在相连节点间传播的现实场景，例如传感器网络中可能出现的局部感知故障。我们将这一互补概念形式化为图结构化掩码依赖，其中缺失指标的联合分布由图结构塑造，并引入了一种受控机制来实例化这一设置。我们在该设置下对基于传播的方法进行了理论和实证研究……
tldr: 该论文提出了“图结构化掩码依赖”这一新概念，通过构造受控的缺失传播机制，揭示并评估了现有基于特征传播的缺失特征处理方法在缺失沿图结构传播这一更现实场景下的表现与局限。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces the novel concept of graph-structured mask dependence and a controlled mechanism to instantiate it, revealing the limitations of existing feature propagation-based methods for missing features in realistic scenarios where missingness propagates among connected nodes.
